tools.description: Put a website live at a public URL. Use this when the user wants to publish, launch, or get a page online — e.g. 'I need a website', 'put up a page for my business', 'make this live'. Takes static files (HTML, CSS, JS, images) and returns a working URL anyone can open. No build step, no config. First call: omit site_id and edit_token — you get back a url, a site_id, and an edit_token. Keep the edit_token; it's the only way to change this site later. Later calls: pass site_id + edit_token to publish over the same site. deploy REPLACES the whole site — any file you leave out is DELETED. To change just one or a few files, use update_site_file instead. To see what's currently live before editing, use get_site_files first.

edit_token.description: Edit token returned at create time. Required to update.

email.description: Email to associate with the site. Captured unverified at first deploy; verification only required later for custom domains and recovery.

files.description: Files to publish. Must include an index.html at the root.

content.description: File body. Text by default; binary must be base64.

encoding.description: Defaults to utf-8 for text extensions, base64 otherwise.

path.description: Path under the site root, e.g. 'index.html', 'assets/logo.png'.

site_id.description: Existing site id to update. Omit to create a new site.

tools.name: deploy

created.description: true if this call created a new site; false if it updated an existing one.

dashboard_url.description: Deep link to this site in the owner's dashboard.

edit_token.description: Returned ONLY on first create. Save it — it's the only way to update this site.

email_masked.description: The owner email, masked for display (e.g. 'a***@example.com').

email_verified.description: Whether the site's owner email is verified right now. New sites are always false.

files_uploaded.description: Number of files written in this deploy.

site_id.description: The site's slug / id — pass back to update it later.

total_bytes.description: Total size of the site in bytes after this deploy.

url.description: The live URL of the published site.

verify_required.description: true when the owner still needs to verify their email (keys on !email_verified).

tools.description: Read the files of a site you already published, so you can make a targeted edit instead of rebuilding the whole site from memory. Returns a complete manifest (every file's path, size, content-type, sha256) plus the contents of the text files (HTML/CSS/JS/etc). Also returns the site's current `version` — pass it back to update_site_file so you don't overwrite a newer change. Pass `paths` to fetch only specific files; omit it to get all text files. Requires site_id + edit_token.

edit_token.description: The edit token returned at publish time.

paths.description: Optional. Specific file paths to return contents for (e.g. ['index.html','style.css']). Omit to get all text files. The manifest always lists every file regardless.

site_id.description: The site id returned at publish time.

tools.name: get_site_files

files.description: Inlined contents of the requested text files (default: all text files, capped for size).

content.description: Full text content of the file.

encoding.description: Always 'utf-8' — only text files are inlined.

path.description: Path of this file under the site root.

manifest.description: Every file on the site (always complete, regardless of which contents were inlined).

is_text.description: Whether the file is a text type eligible to have its content inlined.

path.description: Path under the site root, e.g. 'index.html'.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of the file bytes; null if not recorded for this file.

truncated.description: true if some requested file contents were omitted for size — request specific paths to read them.

url.description: The live URL of the site.

version.description: The site's current version — pass as expected_version to update_site_file to avoid clobbering.

annotations.title: Edit specific files of a published site

tools.description: Change one or a few files of an already-published site, leaving every other file untouched (a merge — unlike deploy, which replaces the whole site). Ideal for small edits: fix a typo in index.html, swap a stylesheet, add one page. Best practice: call get_site_files first, edit the returned content, then call this with the files you changed and the `expected_version` from that read — if the site changed in the meantime you get a clear conflict telling you to re-read. Requires site_id + edit_token. Cannot delete files (use deploy to drop a file) and cannot remove index.html.

edit_token.description: The edit token returned at publish time.

expected_version.description: Optional but recommended. The `version` you got from get_site_files. If the site has changed since, the update is rejected with a conflict so you can re-read and re-apply. Omit to force last-writer-wins.

files.description: The files to change. Only these are written; all other files on the site survive.

content.description: Full new file body. Text by default; binary must be base64.

encoding.description: Defaults to utf-8 for text, base64 otherwise.

path.description: Path under the site root, e.g. 'index.html'.

site_id.description: The site id returned at publish time.

tools.name: update_site_file

files_total.description: Total number of files on the site after the merge.

files_written.description: Paths of the files written in this update. All other files were left untouched.

url.description: The live URL of the site.

version.description: The site's new version after the merge.
